headline: Brighton 3-2 Tottenham: Seagulls complete stunning three-goal second-half blitz to defeat Spurs
whyCareReason: Fabian Hürzeler's Brighton rally from two goals down at halftime to shock Tottenham 3-2, climbing into fourth place in the Premier League.
teaser: FINAL: Brighton 3, Tottenham Hotspur 2. Brennan Johnson and James Maddison give Spurs early control before Yankuba Minteh, Georginio Rutter, and Danny Welbeck score three second-half goals.
story:
Why this one matters: The Amex Stadium erupted into pandemonium on Sunday afternoon as Brighton & Hove Albion authored one of the most remarkable second-half turnarounds in recent Premier League history, fighting back from 2-0 down to stun Tottenham Hotspur 3-2.

Tottenham appeared in cruise control during the opening 45 minutes. Brennan Johnson continued his rich vein of scoring by finishing neatly in the 23rd minute, and James Maddison doubled the lead eight minutes before the interval with a low curling strike. Ange Postecoglou's side looked destined for an easy away victory.

Yet Fabian Hürzeler reshuffled his side at the break, and the Seagulls emerged with fierce intensity. Yankuba Minteh halved the deficit just three minutes into the second half, capitalizing on an errant clearance. Ten minutes later, Georginio Rutter displayed sublime strength and footwork inside the box to drill home an equalizer. In the 66th minute, Rutter crossed for Danny Welbeck, who rose unopposed to power a header past Guglielmo Vicario.

The stunning 3-2 triumph vaults Brighton into fourth place on 14 points, while Tottenham remain stuck in the lower half with only two points from their six games.
stakes: Brighton climb to fourth place in the Premier League with 14 points, while Tottenham remain mired in the bottom spots.
rivalryAngle: Hürzeler out-tactics Postecoglou with bold halftime adjustments, handing Spurs their most painful collapse of the campaign.
